title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — bad tree / bird analogies: infants and unfledged birds still have the nature
pass_a_gloss: Same pattern in the Lord's 'bad tree / bad fruit': unregenerate infants are still bad trees though fruitless yet—just as a newly hatched chick is still a bird though it does not yet fly.
pass_b_english: So when the Lord says every bad tree bears bad fruit, he would gather poorly who denied that the unregenerate infants of unbelievers are bad trees because they do not yet bear bad fruit. No otherwise than if, reading that every bird flies, he concluded that a chick just hatched, because it does not yet fly, is not a bird.
source_text: Sic cum Dominus dicit omnem arborem malam malos ferre fructus, male colligeret qui infidelium irregenitos infantulos malas arbores esse negaret, quod non ferant malos fructus; haud secus certe ac qui legisset, omnem volucrem volare, male inde concluderet, aviculam recens exclusam, quod nondum volet, volucrem non esse.
notes: Cap. IX aptitudo densify section 630 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 352–353 tip).
